summary: Markdown applies a GitHub-like HTML policy during normal rendering. Exceptional fallbacks intentionally fail closed: delimiter/bracket floods use a linear HTML-only scrub instead of CommonMark, whose nested-image parsing remains quadratic even without emphasis; caught render failures scrub text flattened from the already-filtered mdast. In these rare views, every dropped-element, comment, CDATA, declaration or processing-instruction opener hides the remaining text through EOF, including apparent closing delimiters: a closer can be literal code rather than a normal-render boundary. These fallbacks can hide HTML-looking literal code or additional text, never disclose hidden HTML. Raw pre/code retains its words in normal rendering, details disclose, links allow http(s) and document references, images wait for consent, and nesting is capped at 32

replay.detail: Web UI only; no replay or rebuild.

compatibility.detail: Web UI only; no wire, protocol, runtime or client changes.
